title: Geometric connectedness can be checked after a field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension], let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $k'/k$ be a field extension. Regard the base change $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] as a scheme over $k'$ through its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k'$. Then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if $X_{k'}$ is geometrically connected over $k'$.

proof.text: For the converse use geometrically_iff_of_commRing_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms to fix an arbitrary field extension K/k. Obtain a common extension M of k' and K using Field.exists_common_extension [lem-weil-common-extension-fields]. Write a: Spec M → Spec k' and b: Spec M → Spec K for the maps induced by the two algebra embeddings. Their composites to Spec k agree because the embeddings are k-linear. Form T = (X ×_k Spec K) ×_K Spec M. The universal property of the pullback [def-pc-fibre-product] constructs r: T → X ×_k Spec k'. Pasting the two defining pullback squares and cancelling the defining square for X ×_k Spec k' shows that (r, T → Spec M) is a pullback square over Spec k'. The assumed geometric connectedness over k' therefore gives ConnectedSpace T.

proof.text: The map b: Spec M → Spec K is surjective: its source is nonempty and its target is a singleton. Mathlib's base-change stability instance for Surjective makes the first projection p: T → X ×_k Spec K surjective. Apply Function.Surjective.connectedSpace to p.surjective and p.continuous. Since K/k was arbitrary, the commutative-ring criterion for geometrically connected morphisms proves geometric connectedness of X over k.
